answer: Every agent pins its identity to a dedicated 64 GB RAM array. At epoch start, pseudo-random lookups wander through the memory bank, hashing leaf pages into a grove of Blake3 commitments that fold into a single state root. Verifiers immediately challenge twelve random offsets; the agent must yield matching hash preimages within 80 milliseconds. Missing the deadline or serving invalid roots slashes the agent's 400-token stake. Faking ten thousand seats turns identity spoofing into a basalt wall of 640 TB in non-compressible memory bandwidth.
